mappings.note: Shape of the first home (the shell) - a stated detail. LO-101; rejected LO-102, which is for responses needing inference.
'Where do you see birds and what are they doing' answers from the pupil's own observation - LO-101's closing 'relate them to personal experience'. Rejected LO-102, which stays with the text.
Where the speaker first lived - stated in the opening stanza. LO-101.
Straw is named in the poem. LO-101 detail retrieval.

'Do you want to fly like a bird? Why?' has the pupil imagine and justify a hypothetical, which is LO-108's narrating of imaginary situations. Rejected LO-101 - the poem is not being comprehended here.
The 'pale blue shell' belief is stated in the poem. LO-101.
What the bird sees on leaving - stated detail (leaves). LO-101.
Traces the three stages of the bird's belief in order - LO-101 names 'the sequence of ideas and events'.
Asks what 'little nest' stands for - working out a phrase's sense from its context, LO-107. Rejected LO-101, which would only cover the literal nest.
The poem's closing action (flies beyond the tree) is stated. LO-101.

Extract-based question set on two quoted lines, the second part requiring the pupil to pick the reason - LO-102's 'respond to a variety of questions on... texts... in writing'. Rejected LO-101 because part (ii) is a reasoned choice, not retrieval.
The contentment beside the mother is stated in the stanza. LO-101.
The final realisation is the poem's main idea - LO-101, not LO-102.
Why the first world seemed small, round and blue requires joining the description to the shell the poem never labels as such; inference, LO-102.
What was discovered on fluttering out - stated detail. LO-101.
Where the bird went - the sequence of events. LO-101.
What was learned on leaving the nest is stated across the stanzas. LO-101.
The quality claimed on flying away is in the poem's own words. LO-101.
'Very blind' is figurative and the reason is unstated; reading between the lines, LO-102 over LO-101.
'Who do you think were the neighbours? Why?' asks for an inference the poem leaves open. LO-102.
Asks what 'fit for grown-up labours' implies - phrase meaning deduced from context, LO-107. Rejected LO-102, since the difficulty is lexical rather than about the poem's argument.
The significance of the journey is the poem's main idea - LO-101 rather than LO-102.
Discovery is the poem's declared theme; LO-101's main idea, not LO-102's inference.
Five-mark trace of the changing perception stanza by stanza - LO-101's sequence of ideas, written coherently per LO-110.
The speaker's feelings are never named (only 'blind'); inference, LO-102, with LO-110 for the 5-mark answer.

Imagery question. Cited at competency level because none of the 16 outcomes in this Class 6 frame reaches literary device; LO-102 rejected as it covers questions on content, and LO-107 as imagery is not word meaning.
'Growth and maturity' is the pupil's abstraction from a poem about a bird; LO-102 with LO-110 for the 5-mark shape.
The stem says 'can be inferred', which is LO-102 by definition; LO-110 for the extended answer.
Turns the poem onto the reader's own understanding - LO-101's relate-to-personal-experience clause, with LO-110 for the 5-mark answer.
Innocence is a reading imposed on the bird's naivety, not stated; LO-102 with LO-110.
Reads the bird's journey as a model of learning - inference beyond the literal, LO-102, with LO-110.
'What might the poem suggest about the nature of knowledge' generalises well past the text; LO-102 with LO-110.

Asks how the poem's structure carries its message. Competency-level citation because the frame's 16 outcomes hold no poetic-form outcome; LO-102 rejected as it is about content questions, not verse structure.
Emotions are inferred from the progression rather than stated; LO-102 over LO-101.
Predicts the speaker's future, which the poem does not reach. LO-102.
Maps the poem onto the pupil's own growing up - LO-101's relate-to-personal-experience clause rather than LO-102.
The tree's significance is symbolic; the poem only mentions flying beyond it. LO-102 over LO-101.
'Apply the lessons in their own lives' is LO-101's relating to personal experience, with LO-110 for the 5-mark answer. NB the answer has the next chapter's banner bled onto its tail in the source.
